section: Section Three — The Mishnah and the Talmud
subtitle: Rebbi organizes the Oral Torah into the six orders of the Mishnah
author: Moses Maimonides
intro: Rambam's general introduction to his Commentary on the Mishnah — tracing the oral tradition from Sinai through the Zugot, Rebbi's compilation of the Mishnah, the Talmud and Geonim, and his own methodology. Original 12th-century Judeo-Arabic with English translation.

aligned.ja:
בג'מלהֵ אלשראיע, ראי אן יקסם כל ג'נס מנהא
אלי אנואעה עלי מא ילזם, וסמא כל נוע מסכתא.
ת'ם קסם אלקול פי כל נוע אלי פצול סמי כל
פצל פרק. ת'ם קסם אלקול פי כל פצל אלי
פצול אקרב סהלהֵ אלמאכ'ד' לאלחפט'
ואלתעלים וסמי כל פצל מן תלך אלפצול אלצגאר
הלכה.
aligned.en: With the whole body of the laws before him, he saw fit to divide each genus among them into its species as was fitting, and he named each species a *masekhet* (tractate). He then divided the discussion within each species into chapters, naming each chapter a *perek*. He then divided the discussion within each chapter into smaller divisions that would be easier to grasp for memorization and teaching, and he named each of those small divisions a *halakha*.

וקסם אלקול פי סדר זרעים עלי מא אצן,
אול מא בדא בברכות ועלהֵ ד'לך אן אלטביב
אלמאהר אד'י אראד חרז צחהֵ אלצחיח עלי מא
הו עליה, פאול מא יתקדם בצלאח אלגד'א,
פלד'לך ראי הד'א אלמויד באלחק אן יבתדי
בברכות, לאן כל מן יאכל לא יקדר יאכל
חתי יבארך, פראי אן אחק מא יבדא בה אלכלאם
פי אלברכות ליצלח אלגד'א אצלאחא מענויא.
aligned.en: He divided the discussion within Seder Zeraim—as I reckon—beginning first with Berakhot. The reason for this is as follows: a skilled physician who wishes to preserve a healthy man's health as it is begins first with the proper regulation of his diet; and so this man, upheld by the truth, saw fit to begin with Berakhot, since no one who eats may eat until he has recited a blessing. He therefore judged that the most fitting thing with which to begin his discourse was the blessings, so as to set the "diet" right in a spiritual sense.

ת'ם ראי באן לא יכון אלכלאם פי גרץ' מן
אלאגראץ' נאקצא, בל יתכלם עלי ג'מלת
אלברכות אללאזמה לאלאגד'יה ואלשראיע, וליס
ת'ם שריעה לאזמה לכל רג'ל כל יום אלא
קרית שמע פקט, וליס מן אלאתקאן אן יתכלם
פי ברכות קרית שמע קבל אן יתכלם פי
קרית שמע נפסהא, פבדא מאמתי קורין את
שמע ומא אתצל בד'לך.
aligned.en: He then judged that the discussion of any one of his topics should not be left deficient, but that he should treat the whole body of blessings required for foods and for the commandments. Now the only commandment binding upon every man each day is the recitation of the Shema alone; and it would not be methodical to discuss the blessings of the Shema before discussing the Shema itself. He therefore began, *From what time may one recite the Shema* (M. Berakhot 1:1), together with what is connected to it.

ת'ם רג'ע אלי גרץ'
אלסדר והו אלכלאם פי שראיע נבאת אלארץ'
פבדא במסכת פאה בעד ברכות, לאן ג'מיע
אלחקוק אלד'י תלזם אלזרע אנמא תלזמה בעד
חצדה ואלפאה תלזם אלסנבל והו פי אלארץ',
פלד'לך קדם אלקול פיהא.
aligned.en: He then returned to the purpose of the order, namely the discussion of the laws of the produce of the earth, and so he began with tractate Pe'ah after Berakhot. For all the dues that fall upon a crop fall upon it only after it has been reaped, whereas Pe'ah falls upon the standing grain while it is still in the ground; for this reason he placed its discussion first.

aligned.en: After Pe'ah comes Demai, since the poor too have a right in it, just as they have in Pe'ah, as they said, *One may feed the poor with demai* (M. Demai 3:1).

aligned.en: After Demai comes Kil'ayim, for this is the sequence the verse follows in *You shall be holy* (Lev 19:2 ff.): *You shall not finish off the corner of your field* (Lev 19:9), and after it *You shall not sow your field with mixed kinds* (Lev 19:19).

אנה ראי אן אלערלה ליסת צ'רוריה לאן טאל
מא לם יגרס לא תלזמה ערלה ואלשביעית
צ'רוריה, ות'ם אן אלשמטה פיהא סדר מן
אלתורה מג'רד, פלד'לך קדם אלקול פי אלשמטה.
aligned.en: Then after Kil'ayim comes Shevi'it. It would have been proper for tractate Orla to come after Kil'ayim, for that is the sequence of Scripture, were it not that he judged Orla not to be of pressing necessity—for so long as a man does not plant, Orla does not apply to him—whereas Shevi'it is of pressing necessity, and moreover the release of debts in it is a plain ordinance of the Torah; for this reason he placed the discussion of the sabbatical year first.

pairs.en: Then after Kil'ayim comes Shevi'it

ומן בעד שביעית מסכת תרומה, לאנהא אעני

אלתרומה מעשר ראשון, לאנה אלתאלי
לאלתרומה פי אלאכ'ראג'. ומן בעד מעשר ראשון
מעשר שני עלי אלרתבה.
aligned.en: After Shevi'it comes tractate Teruma, since the teruma—I mean the heave-offering—is the first due taken from the crop. After Teruma comes Ma'aser Rishon, since it is what follows teruma in the order of separation. After Ma'aser Rishon comes Ma'aser Sheni, in sequence.

לאן בעד אן יכ'רג' מן אלזרע הד'ה אלחקוק

שני חיניד' יטחן ויצנע מנה דקיק ויעג'ן

aligned.en: After it comes tractate Challa, for once these dues we have described—teruma, ma'aser rishon, and ma'aser sheni—have been taken from the crop, it is then ground, made into flour, kneaded, and becomes liable to challa.

pairs.en: After it comes tractate Challa

פלמא תם אלכלאם עלי אלזרע
וחקוקה, אכ'ד' טי אלכלאם עלי אלת'מאר פבעד
אלחלה תכלם עלי אלערלה. ת'ם עלי אלבכורים
עלי רתבהֵ אלנץ' אלערלה פי ויקרא ואלבכורים
פי והיה כי תבוא, פאנתהא פי תקסים אלקול פי
זרעים אחדי עשרהֵ מסכתא.
aligned.en: Once the discussion of the crop and its dues was complete, he took up the thread of discussion concerning the fruits, and so after Challa he discussed Orla, then Bikkurim, following the sequence of the verse: Orla in *Leviticus* (Lev 19:23), and Bikkurim in *And it shall be when you come* (Deut 26:1 ff.). Thus the division of the discussion in Zeraim came to eleven tractates.

ת'ם אכ'ד' פי קסמהֵ סדר מועד אלי אנואעה
איצ'א עלי מא עמל פי זרעים, פאבתדא במסכת
שבת לקדמה פי אלשרף, ת'ם אנה כל סבעהֵ
איאם פיכת'ר דורה פי אלזמאן, ובה איצ'א
בדא אלכתאב פי אול אלאעיאד.
aligned.en: He then took up the division of Seder Moed into its species as well, just as he had done with Zeraim, and began with tractate Shabbat, on account of its precedence in honor, and because it recurs every seven days, so that its cycle within time is frequent; and it is also with Shabbat that Scripture begins among the festivals.

pairs.en: He then took up the division of Seder Moed into its species

ערובין לאנהא מן גרץ' אלשבת. ובעדהא בפסחים

והי איצ'א אלתאליה לשבת פי פרשת מועדות.
aligned.en: After Shabbat comes Eruvin, since it pertains to the purpose of Shabbat. After it comes Pesachim, since it is the first commandment legislated through Moses, and it is also what follows Shabbat in the portion of the appointed times (Lev 23).

He had already discussed Pesachim, so there remained for him to discuss Sukkot and Shavuot; but there was nothing he had to treat regarding Shavuot beyond matters common to every festival day, namely tractate Beitzah. He therefore placed Sukkah before Beitzah, on account of the many laws of Sukkot.
